Yes: DeCode: Decoupling Content and Delivery for Medical QA by Po-Jen Ko, Chen-Han Tsai, and Yu-Shao Peng matches that idea directly. It presents a training-free, model-agnostic framework that decouples content and delivery to produce contextualized answers in clinical settings, and reports improved medical question answering performance on HealthBench [1].

If you meant related medical QA work, other papers here focus more on retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, or multi-hop reasoning rather than decoupling content and delivery [2, 7, 8, 9].
